name: Generic YF-S201 / ZJ-S201 1/2-inch hall-effect water flow sensor, no named maker (LaskaKit LA131042, Botland 5904422366933)
//: Written by /spark:research on 2026-09-29 as a CATALOG record, from two Czech shop listings and nothing else: LaskaKit's 'YF-S201 průtokoměr vody 1-30L/min' and Botland's 'Snímač průtoku kapaliny YF-S201 30 l/m - závit' (whose description calls the same item ZJ-S201). 'YF-S201' is a model name shared across factories, not a part: DFRobot's own SEN0217 is a YF-S201 labelled by 'Sea/帝江', and Botland names Seeed Studio 314150005 'G1/2 Water Flow Sensor' as the maker of its unit and links wiki.seeedstudio.com for it (see facts.maker; those Seeed pages were NOT fetched, so nothing here comes from them). There is no maker's datasheet. Where the two listings agree a fact is recorded as the listing's own text; where they disagree — supply range, accuracy, body size, signal-wire colour — it is recorded unverified with both figures, because a seller's copy for a maker-less part is exactly the kind of number that gets promoted to a fact by accident.
//why_not: not the DFRobot SKU; no datasheet
variant: whatever unit LaskaKit (LA131042) or Botland (EAN 5904422366933) ships under the name; two listings, two sets of numbers
//sources: Both fetched on 2026-09-29. LaskaKit's 'Návod v angl.' link is an Instructables tutorial (https://www.instructables.com/id/How-to-Use-Water-Flow-Sensor-Arduino-Tutorial/), not a manual, and its 'Certifikace' is a CE/RoHS zip — neither was fetched or cited. Botland links Seeed's store page (https://www.seeedstudio.com/G1%262%22-Water-Flow-Sensor-p-635.html) and two Seeed wiki pages (http://wiki.seeedstudio.com/G1_and_2_inch_Water_Flow_Sensor/, http://wiki.seeedstudio.com/wiki/G1/2_Water_Flow_sensor) as the maker's documentation — not fetched, because Seeed is the project's second vendor and DFRobot had a fit; they are where a Seeed record would start.

needs.note: The pulse wire. LaskaKit calls the output '5V TTL' and gives 450 pulses per litre or f(Hz) = 7.5 x Q(L/min); Botland says the pulse wire is YELLOW, where DFRobot's YF-S201 has a green one. A 5 V pulse needs a divider or level shifter before a 3.3 V GPIO.

power.note: Red wire per Botland. LaskaKit says 5-18 V DC, Botland 3.5-24 V; both include 5 V, neither includes 3.3 V. 15 mA at 5 V per both.

//pin_order: Empty on purpose: neither listing shows the plug or numbers its positions. Botland lists the wires red, black, yellow in its text, which is a list, not a housing order.
footprint_note: Neither listing shows or names the plug on the lead; Botland's Q&A answer says the ~157 mm cable length is 'including the plug', so there is one. Until a unit is measured, no footprint can be named.

body_mm.why_it_matters: This would be the mating header's outline on the board, which nobody can name until the plug is measured. The sensor's own size is in facts.envelope_mm, and the two listings disagree on it.

sensing_principle.value: hall probe on a magnet-carrying rotor
sensing_principle.note: LaskaKit: 'za pomoci Hallovy sondy'; Botland: 'ventilátoru s magnetem a Hallových senzorů', and that the electronics never touch the water. Both sellers say hall effect, which DFRobot says of SEN0217 and not of SEN0550.

thread_standard.note: LaskaKit: 'Závit: G 1/2"'. Botland says only 'Montáž na trubku o průměru 1/2"' — no standard. A seller's word for a maker-less part; trial-fit a G1/2 coupling anyway.

flow_range_l_min.note: LaskaKit 'Měřený průtok: 1 ~ 30 litrů / m'; Botland 'Rozsah měření: 1 až 30 l/min'. Agree, and match DFRobot's SEN0217.

max_pressure_mpa.note: LaskaKit 'Max. pracovní tlak: 1.75MPa'; Botland 'Přípustný tlak vody: 1,75 MPa'. Agree.

operating_current_ma.note: LaskaKit 'Max. spotřeba: 15mA'; Botland 'Spotřeba proudu pro 5V: 15 mA'. Agree.

max_temperature_c.note: LaskaKit: liquid up to 80 C, 'Max. pracovní teplota: do 80°C'; Botland: 'Provozní teplota: až 80 °C'. Both give 35-90 % RH. Agree with each other; DFRobot's SEN0217 says 120 C for the liquid.

supply_range_v.why_it_matters: The two listings disagree: LaskaKit 'Napájení: 5-18VDC', Botland 'Napájecí napětí: 3,5 V až 24 V' (and 'červená - napájecí napětí od 3,5 V do 24 V'). Both include 5 V and neither includes 3.3 V, so a 5 V rail is safe under either; the maximum a unit survives is whichever seller's unit you got.

output_type.note: LaskaKit's words, 'Výstup: 5V TTL'; Botland says only 'pulzní výstupní signál'. Read as: a pulse at the supply level when supplied with 5 V — the same 3.3 V problem as the DFRobot SKUs. Whether it is open-collector with a pull-up or push-pull is stated by neither (output_stage).

output_stage.source: stated by neither listing; no maker's datasheet exists for a generic unit
output_stage.why_it_matters: Whether a host pull-up to 3.3 V could replace a divider. Unknown here as for SEN0217; a divider or level shifter is the only safe reading.

pulses_per_litre.note: LaskaKit: 'Charakteristika pulzů: 450 pulzů/litr nebo f (Hz) = 7,5* průtok (l/min)'. Botland gives no K-factor. Same nominal figure as DFRobot's SEN0217.

accuracy_pct.why_it_matters: Three numbers for one model name: LaskaKit 'Přesnost měření: 2%', Botland 'nejedná se o přesný senzor ... přesnost není větší než 10 %' (not a precise sensor, no better than 10 %), DFRobot +/- 5 % for its SEN0217. Whether litres can be trusted depends on which is true of the unit in hand — calibrate against a bucket.

envelope_mm.why_it_matters: The two listings disagree by a few millimetres and DFRobot's SEN0217 says 62 x 36 x 35; enough for a pipe run, not for an enclosure cut-out. Botland's package is 80 x 96 x 36 mm, 52 g; LaskaKit's unit weighs 51 g.

cable_length_mm.note: LaskaKit 'Délka kabelu: ~15cm'; Botland's answer to a customer question (2022): 'Celková délka kabelu včetně zástrčky je přibližně 157 mm' — total including the plug about 157 mm. Agree within a centimetre. Short: the enclosure has to be at the pipe, or the lead extended.

wire_colours.value: red = supply, black = ground, yellow = pulse (Botland); LaskaKit does not say
wire_colours.why_it_matters: Which wire is the signal. Botland's unit has a yellow pulse wire where DFRobot's YF-S201 has a green one, so the colour is not a property of the model name — read the unit's own wires, and never wire a header from this record without it.

lead_connector.source: shown or named by neither listing; Botland's Q&A answer says the cable length is 'including the plug', so there is one
lead_connector.why_it_matters: It decides the host footprint (footprint_note). Unknown until a unit is measured.

maker.source: LaskaKit's brand field says 'LaskaKit_cz' and names no maker; Botland's description says 'Webové stránky výrobce: Seeedstudio 314150005' and links https://www.seeedstudio.com/G1%262%22-Water-Flow-Sensor-p-635.html and http://wiki.seeedstudio.com/G1_and_2_inch_Water_Flow_Sensor/ — not fetched
maker.why_it_matters: A maker means a datasheet, and Botland's claim would make its unit Seeed's G1/2 Water Flow Sensor, the project's second vendor, with a wiki of its own. If that is confirmed, this record should become a Seeed record with Seeed's numbers, and every disagreement above gets a source to settle it.

host_requirements: A 5 V pulse ('5V TTL' in LaskaKit's words) into a 3.3 V GPIO needs a divider or a level shifter; neither listing says whether a host pull-up alone would do.
Feed it from the 5 V rail: both listings include 5 V and neither includes 3.3 V; they disagree on the maximum (18 V or 24 V), so do not feed it 24 V on Botland's word if the unit came from LaskaKit.
Read the unit's own wires before building a header: Botland's pulse wire is yellow, DFRobot's YF-S201's is green, and nobody has shown the plug.
Accuracy is 2 %, 5 % or 'no better than 10 %' depending on who is describing the same model name; calibrate against a bucket if litres matter.
The lead is about 15 cm: the enclosure sits at the pipe or the lead gets extended, and an extended 5 V pulse line picks up noise.

sourcing.note: LA131042, 98 Kč with VAT (81 Kč without), 17 in stock, deliverable by 2026-10-02 per the page.
EAN 5904422366933; 120 CZK from the page's price metadata; stock not read; customer rating 4.8/5 from 9 reviews.
